newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine provinces reject nuclear waste dumps.
newsitem.headline: Argentine provinces reject nuclear waste dumps.

text.p: A new law authorizing nuclear waste dumps in Argentina was rejected by most of the country's provinces, the newspaper La Nacion said Tuesday.

"Our best guarantee (against nuclear dumps) is the provincial constitution...which totally bans nuclear testing and the storage of uranium and other dangerous materials and waste," La Nacion quoted Diego Gorvein, deputy of the ruling Peronist party in north-eastern Formosa province, as saying.
The parliaments of several provinces with areas considered by the government as possible sites for nuclear dumps have clearly rejected this possibility in their legislation.

Last Wednesday, the Peronist Senate majority voted into law a bill allowing the privatization of two nuclear power stations and one unfinished plant and authorizing nuclear waste to be dumped on Argentine soil.
The measure was opposed by legislators from the opposition Radical party as well as by provincial parties and environmental organizations such as Greenpeace, which described it as "outrageous."
The government hopes to raise $200 million through the privatizations, which have already been penciled into this year's budget.
